title: Remote Work Policy Database
demand_signal: Strong and validated. 91% of job seekers ask about remote work options during interviews, and 84% are willing to reject offers without flexible arrangements. Remote hiring delivers 340% larger candidate pools. Scoop Technologies tracks 9,000+ company policies but data is not publicly accessible/searchable for individual job seekers.
target_audience: Job seekers, recruiters, HR professionals, remote work advocates, career coaches, salary negotiation consultants, and talent acquisition teams
public_data_sources: Company career pages (remote work policy sections)
LinkedIn company pages and job postings
News articles covering major policy shifts (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, etc.)
Glassdoor company reviews mentioning WFH policies
Indeed and other job board postings with remote/hybrid tags
competitive_landscape: Scoop Technologies' Flex Index tracks 9,000+ companies but is not a public-facing search tool for consumers. FlexJobs, We Work Remotely, and Remote.co focus on job listings, not policy databases. No affordable, searchable, consumer-facing database exists. This is a clear market gap with strong demand.
monetization_model: Freemium: Free basic search by company name or industry. Premium tier ($9.99-19.99/mo) includes advanced filters (days required in office, full remote vs hybrid, location flexibility), CSV exports, email alerts for policy changes, and API access for recruiters.
estimated_market_size: 65% of US companies offer hybrid work, 18% are fully remote. Target audience: 160M+ US workers, 20M+ active job seekers. TAM for premium subscriptions: $50-100M annually (assuming 0.1% conversion of active job seekers at $120/year).
data_freshness_requirement: Monthly updates minimum. Quarterly deep refreshes. Real-time updates for major companies (Fortune 500) via news monitoring.
compliance_notes: PASS potential: All data is publicly disclosed corporate policy information. No PII. No employee-level data. Companies publicly announce these policies for recruitment purposes. Source attribution via company career page URLs.
next_steps: Build initial dataset: Top 500 companies with verified policies
Create simple search interface (company name, industry, HQ location)
Pilot with free tier to validate demand
Add premium filters based on user feedback
Build automated scraper for career page policy sections
researcher_notes: This is the strongest signal from today's scan. The gap is crystal clear: job seekers desperately need this information, existing trackers (Scoop) don't serve consumers, and all data is public. The 3-day office week (76% of hybrid companies use 3-2 model) has become standard, making this data highly structured and comparable. Strike while policy changes are still frequent and newsworthy.
